title: Gluten-Free Lemon Cornmeal Waffles
changes_from_base: Potato starch and wholegrain cornmeal replace the wheat flour, lots of lemon zest goes into the milk, and the batter rests 10 minutes so the cornmeal softens.
summary: Light, tangy waffles made with cornmeal and potato starch, lifted by plenty of fresh lemon zest.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron and put a wire rack set in a baking tray into a 95°C oven.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk 74 g potato starch, 103 g cornmeal, 35 g caster sugar, 1½ tsp baking powder and ½ tsp fine salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In a second bowl whisk 2 eggs, 57 g melted butter, 220 ml milk and 2 tbsp lemon zest.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the wet mixture to the dry ingredients, stir together, then leave the batter to rest for 10 min.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Brush the hot iron lightly with oil and cook the waffles until golden.

steps.title: Hold
steps.text: Keep cooked waffles warm on the rack in the oven while you cook the rest.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Freeze any leftovers for a few weeks and reheat in a toaster.

tips: Use a fine grater to zest the lemons so the batter doesn't turn bitter from the pith.
Check the cornmeal and baking powder are labelled gluten-free if that matters to your guests.
Swap the melted butter for 35 g vegetable oil if you prefer a dairy-free batter.
storage: Freeze any leftover waffles for a few weeks and reheat them in a toaster. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
